title: BQP versus BPP
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Prove or disprove that bounded-error polynomial-time quantum computation can solve a decision problem that no bounded-error polynomial-time classical algorithm can solve, without an oracle.
status: Open since the formulation of quantum complexity theory. Oracle separations and candidate applications do not establish the unrelativized separation.
why: Establishes whether quantum computers fundamentally enlarge efficient computation.
key_works: John Watrous (2008), *Quantum Computational Complexity*, arXiv:0804.3401.

title: NP-complete problems in BQP
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Determine whether NP is contained in BQP; equivalently, whether a quantum computer can solve an NP-complete decision problem in polynomial time.
status: Open. Grover-type improvements concern search complexity and do not give polynomial-time algorithms for unrestricted NP-complete problems.
why: Determines whether quantum computing can efficiently solve general combinatorial search rather than selected structured problems.
key_works: Watrous (2008), *Quantum Computational Complexity*, arXiv:0804.3401.

title: The unrelativized relationship between BQP and PH
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Determine whether BQP is contained in the polynomial hierarchy, whether PH is contained in BQP, or whether they are incomparable.
status: Oracle evidence separates quantum computation from PH, but it does not resolve these containments for ordinary computation.
why: Locates quantum computation relative to classical alternation and approximate counting.
key_works: Scott Aaronson (2010), *BQP and the polynomial hierarchy*, DOI:10.1145/1806689.1806711; Ran Raz and Avishay Tal (2019), *Oracle separation of BQP and PH*, DOI:10.1145/3313276.3316315.

title: Perfect completeness for QMA
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Determine whether QMA equals QMA₁ for a specified standard finite gate set: can every valid instance have a witness accepted with certainty?
status: Open. Recent amplification results improve completeness dramatically but also establish black-box limitations; arbitrarily small error is not perfect completeness.
why: Clarifies the role of unavoidable verification error in quantum proofs.
key_works: Scott Aaronson, Phillip Harris, and Freek Witteveen (2025; revised 2026), *Limits to black-box amplification in QMA*, arXiv:2509.21131.

title: Quantum Valiant–Vazirani isolation
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Construct a randomized polynomial-time reduction from general QMA verification to verification with a unique accepting quantum witness, with suitable completeness and soundness promises.
status: Open for unrestricted QMA. Classical and restricted quantum analogues do not provide a general quantum witness-isolation theorem.
why: Would transfer uniqueness-based algorithms and hardness arguments into quantum complexity.
key_works: Dorit Aharonov, Michael Ben-Or, Fernando Brandão, and Or Sattath (2008), *The Pursuit of Uniqueness: Extending Valiant-Vazirani Theorem to the Probabilistic and Quantum Settings*, arXiv:0810.4840.

title: Error reduction for StoqMA
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Determine whether StoqMA verification admits general efficient error reduction while preserving its restricted computational structure.
status: Open since StoqMA’s introduction. Aharonov–Grilo–Liu show that suitable error reduction would imply StoqMA = MA.
why: Tests whether stoquastic verification genuinely exceeds classical randomized verification.
key_works: Dorit Aharonov, Alex B. Grilo, and Yupan Liu (2020/2025), *StoqMA vs. MA: the power of error reduction*, arXiv:2010.02835; DOI:10.22331/q-2025-09-11-1853.

title: General commuting local Hamiltonians in NP
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Determine whether every bounded-locality commuting local Hamiltonian problem has polynomial-size classical certificates for its low-energy promise.
status: Open generally. Bostanci–Hwang’s 2026 results extend NP containment to important rank-one cases beyond two dimensions, but not arbitrary commuting interactions.
why: Separates computational difficulty caused by noncommutativity from difficulty caused by entanglement.
key_works: John Bostanci and Yeongwoo Hwang (2026), *Commuting Local Hamiltonians Beyond 2D*, DOI:10.4230/LIPIcs.ITCS.2026.25.

title: No low-energy samplable states
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Construct local Hamiltonian families for which every sufficiently low-energy state escapes the relevant efficient classical sampling-description class, as formalized by the NLSS conjecture.
status: Open beyond restricted state families. Exclusions of Clifford, almost-Clifford, and fermionic Gaussian low-energy states are partial results, not the full claim.
why: Strengthens the evidence that low-energy quantum matter cannot be represented by tractable classical models.
key_works: Kartik Anand (2025), *Constructing Fermionic Hamiltonians with Non-Gaussianic low-energy states*, arXiv:2502.15368.

title: Maximum randomized-versus-quantum separation for total functions
subfield: Quantum query complexity and algebraic algorithms
open: Determine the optimal exponent relating randomized query complexity \(R(f)\) and bounded-error quantum query complexity \(Q(f)\) for total Boolean functions.
status: The general gap between known large separations and upper bounds remains unresolved; the 2025 survey records cubic-type separations versus a quartic general upper bound.
why: Measures quantum speedup without hiding difficulty in a promise.
key_works: Yassine Hamoudi (2025), *A Brief Introduction to Quantum Query Complexity*, arXiv:2508.08852; Aaronson (2021), *Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity*, arXiv:2109.06917.

title: Optimal quantum complexity of k-distinctness
subfield: Quantum query complexity and algebraic algorithms
open: Obtain matching quantum query upper and lower bounds for detecting a value occurring at least \(k\) times, for each fixed \(k\geq3\), and understand growing \(k\).
status: Open beyond element distinctness. Learning graphs and multidimensional quantum walks improve algorithms, but do not settle the complete exponent landscape.
why: Tests the limits of quantum walks and collision-finding techniques.
key_works: Stacey Jeffery and Sebastian Zur (2022), *Multidimensional Quantum Walks, with Application to k-Distinctness*, arXiv:2208.13492.

title: Computational complexity of Uhlmann transformations
subfield: Quantum query complexity and algebraic algorithms
open: Characterize when a unitary mapping between compatible purifications can be synthesized efficiently, especially for succinctly specified mixed states without privileged purification access.
status: Structural completeness and equivalence results exist; efficient synthesis for important promised families remains unresolved.
why: Connects quantum state conversion, cryptography, and recovery of encoded information.
key_works: John Bostanci, Yuval Efron, Tony Metger, Alexander Poremba, Luowen Qian, and Henry Yuen (2023), *Unitary Complexity and the Uhlmann Transformation Problem*, arXiv:2306.13073.

title: Permanent anticoncentration
open: Prove sufficiently strong lower-tail bounds for the permanent of a Gaussian matrix, at its natural \(\sqrt{n!}\) scale, to support approximate-sampling reductions.
status: Open in the required general form. This is distinct from proving that permanent estimation is computationally hard.
why: Converts additive probability-estimation information into useful multiplicative information.
key_works: Aaronson and Arkhipov (2011), *The Computational Complexity of Linear Optics*, arXiv:1011.3245.

title: Average-case hafnian hardness for Gaussian boson sampling
open: Establish the average-case hardness and anticoncentration statements needed for the experimentally relevant Gaussian-boson-sampling distributions, including their structured matrix ensembles.
status: Open in robust approximate-sampling formulations. Exact hafnian hardness alone does not settle noisy experimental distributions.
why: Places Gaussian photonic advantage on firmer complexity foundations.
key_works: Craig S. Hamilton et al. (2017), *Gaussian Boson Sampling*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.119.170501; Daniel Grier et al. (2022), *The Complexity of Bipartite Gaussian Boson Sampling*.

title: Robust average-case hardness of random-circuit sampling
open: Prove sampling hardness under experimentally meaningful constant total-variation error using defensible average-case assumptions, rather than only exact or extremely high-precision probability estimation.
status: Open at the strongest useful noise-robust level. Existing worst-to-average-case reductions do not automatically deliver that statement.
why: Distinguishes a mathematical hardness theorem from an extrapolation to noisy devices.
key_works: Adam Bouland, Bill Fefferman, Chinmay Nirkhe, and Umesh Vazirani (2018), *Quantum Supremacy and the Complexity of Random Circuit Sampling*, arXiv:1803.04402.

title: Sharp state- and observable-dependent Trotter error bounds
open: Obtain efficiently evaluable error bounds that exploit the actual initial state and measured observable, and that remain predictive at useful simulation times.
status: General commutator-based product-formula bounds are established; tight instance-specific certificates remain substantially less developed.
why: Could remove large safety margins without silently sacrificing accuracy.
key_works: Andrew Childs, Yuan Su, Minh C. Tran, Nathan Wiebe, and Shuchen Zhu (2021), *A Theory of Trotter Error*, arXiv:1912.08854; DOI:10.1103/PhysRevX.11.011020.

title: Certified FeMoco spin-state and energy ordering
open: Compute chemically decisive FeMoco energy differences with a complete uncertainty budget covering the electronic Hamiltonian, active space, state preparation, and quantum numerical error.
status: Resource-estimation studies establish plausible computational routes, not a certified solution of the relevant chemical ordering.
why: Tests quantum computing on a scientifically consequential strongly correlated system.
key_works: Markus Reiher, Nathan Wiebe, Krysta Svore, Dave Wecker, and Matthias Troyer (2017), *Elucidating Reaction Mechanisms on Quantum Computers*, arXiv:1605.03590.

title: Controlled low-temperature phase diagram of the doped Hubbard model
open: Resolve specified competing phases and correlations of the two-dimensional doped Hubbard model with thermodynamic-limit and low-temperature error control.
status: Extensive classical benchmarks constrain portions of the diagram; quantum simulation must still demonstrate controlled answers in the disputed regimes.
why: Tests proposed microscopic explanations of correlated-electron phenomena.
key_works: J. P. F. LeBlanc et al. (2015), *Solutions of the Two Dimensional Hubbard Model: Benchmarks and Results from a Wide Range of Numerical Algorithms*, arXiv:1505.02290.

title: Real-time nonabelian gauge dynamics near the continuum
open: Compute a nontrivial real-time SU(3) observable with controlled errors from lattice spacing, finite volume, electric-field truncation, state preparation, and quantum execution.
status: Lower-dimensional and truncated demonstrations are context, not a complete continuum-QCD calculation.
why: Could address scattering, hadronization, and nonequilibrium strong-interaction physics.
key_works: Bauer et al. (2022), *Quantum Simulation for High Energy Physics*, arXiv:2204.03381; Jordan, Lee, and Preskill (2012), *Quantum Algorithms for Quantum Field Theories*, arXiv:1111.3633.

title: Fixed-angle QAOA conjectures
open: Prove or refute the fixed-angle performance conjectures for QAOA on regular MaxCut graph families, with explicit depth and graph-size dependence.
status: Open conjectural territory beyond analytically solved shallow cases and numerical evidence.
why: Would replace expensive instance-by-instance parameter searches with justified reusable schedules.
key_works: Jonathan Wurtz and Danylo Lykov (2021), *Fixed-angle conjectures for the Quantum Approximate Optimization Algorithm on regular MaxCut graphs*, Physical Review A 104, 052419.

title: Valid confidence intervals for adaptive classical shadows
subfield: Quantum machine learning and learning quantum systems
open: Produce tight confidence guarantees when observables are selected after inspecting shadow data, with realistic measurement errors and repeated adaptive queries.
status: Standard shadow guarantees cover important predetermined-observable settings; unrestricted adaptive reuse needs additional control.
why: Prevents exploratory quantum experiments from reporting selection-biased discoveries.
key_works: Hsin-Yuan Huang, Richard Kueng, and John Preskill (2020), *Predicting Many Properties of a Quantum System from Very Few Measurements*, arXiv:2002.08953.

title: SIC measurements in every finite dimension
subfield: Quantum information, entanglement, and channel capacities
open: Prove that a symmetric informationally complete POVM exists in every finite Hilbert-space dimension, or identify a counterexample dimension.
status: Open. Exact and numerical constructions in many dimensions do not establish the universal statement.
why: Would provide a uniform optimal geometric structure for informationally complete quantum measurements.
key_works: Joseph Renes et al. (2004), *Symmetric informationally complete quantum measurements*; Paweł Horodecki, Łukasz Rudnicki, and Karol Życzkowski (2020), *Five open problems in theory of quantum information*, arXiv:2002.03233.

title: Four mutually unbiased bases in dimension six
subfield: Quantum information, entanglement, and channel capacities
open: Construct four mutually unbiased orthonormal bases of \(\mathbb C^6\), or prove that no such quartet exists.
status: Open. Three are available; the prime-power construction of complete sets does not settle dimension six.
why: Probes the arithmetic obstruction behind optimal complementary measurements.
key_works: Horodecki, Rudnicki, and Życzkowski (2020), *Five open problems in theory of quantum information*, arXiv:2002.03233.

title: Exact two-way capacity of thermal-loss channels
subfield: Quantum information, entanglement, and channel capacities
open: Close the gap between achievable rates and upper bounds for entanglement or secret-key generation through thermal-loss bosonic channels with two-way classical communication.
status: Exact pure-loss benchmarks are established; thermal noise leaves important capacity gaps.
why: Determines the ultimate value of quantum repeaters and transducers in realistic optical links.
key_works: Stefano Pirandola, Riccardo Laurenza, Carlo Ottaviani, and Leonardo Banchi (2017), *Fundamental Limits of Repeaterless Quantum Communications*, arXiv:1510.08863.

title: Low-overhead fault-tolerant blind delegation
open: Demonstrate useful delegated computation that simultaneously preserves input and program privacy, detects cheating, and tolerates physical noise at competitive total overhead.
status: Universal blind computation and theoretical fault-tolerant extensions already exist; the unresolved target is integrated useful-scale performance.
why: Enables confidential use of remote quantum hardware.
key_works: Anne Broadbent, Joseph Fitzsimons, and Elham Kashefi (2009), *Universal blind quantum computation*, arXiv:0807.4154; DOI:10.1109/FOCS.2009.36.

title: Finite-size qLDPC computation advantage
open: Demonstrate a complete finite-size computation where a quantum LDPC architecture uses fewer total physical resources than a well-optimized surface-code implementation at the same failure probability.
status: Low-overhead memory designs and simulations are strong partial results; memory savings do not automatically survive universal gates and routing.
why: Tests whether high-rate codes reduce the cost of actual computation.
key_works: Sergey Bravyi et al. (2024), *High-threshold and low-overhead fault-tolerant quantum memory*, arXiv:2308.07915; DOI:10.1038/s41586-024-07107-7.

title: Fault tolerance against radiation-induced correlated bursts
open: Determine and experimentally validate architecture-level conditions under which measured radiation-induced error bursts can be detected, contained, and corrected without a persistent logical-error floor.
status: Catastrophic correlated bursts have been observed; shielding or average error reduction alone is not a full fault-tolerance argument.
why: A rare chip-wide event can defeat codes designed around local faults.
key_works: Matt McEwen et al. (2022), *Resolving catastrophic error bursts from cosmic rays in large arrays of superconducting qubits*, arXiv:2104.05219.

title: Fault-tolerant quantum random-access memory
open: Build a coherently addressable memory with quantified query fidelity and total hardware, routing, initialization, and correction costs that preserve an application-level advantage.
status: QRAM architectures date to 2007–2008; asymptotic query depth does not establish scalable fault-tolerant feasibility.
why: Many attractive algorithms assume coherent data access that dominates their practical cost.
key_works: Vittorio Giovannetti, Seth Lloyd, and Lorenzo Maccone (2008), *Quantum random access memory*, arXiv:0708.1879.

title: Autonomous bosonic correction during computation
subfield: Passive memories, bosonic codes, and qudits
open: Combine autonomous stabilization with a useful gate set, measurement, and reset while demonstrating that the complete process outperforms an unencoded implementation.
status: Autonomous stabilization and beyond-break-even memories are partial milestones; useful computation requires compatible operations.
why: Could reduce fast classical-feedback requirements.
key_works: Sivak et al. (2023), *Real-time quantum error correction beyond break-even*, arXiv:2211.09116; Réglade et al. (2024), *Quantum control of a cat qubit with bit-flip times exceeding ten seconds*.

title: High-throughput shuttling through large ion-trap networks
open: Route ions through many junctions with bounded heating, loss, timing variation, and congestion while supporting continuous parallel computation.
status: Quantum-CCD and racetrack architectures demonstrate essential primitives, not arbitrary-scale transport reliability.
why: Converts long-lived isolated qubits into a scalable connected processor.
key_works: J. M. Pino et al. (2021), *Demonstration of the trapped-ion quantum-CCD computer architecture*, arXiv:2003.01293; S. A. Moses et al. (2023), *A Race Track Trapped-Ion Quantum Processor*, arXiv:2305.03828.

title: Continuous loading during error-corrected computation
open: Replenish lost atoms while executing repeated syndrome extraction and logical gates, without disturbing stored information or invalidating calibration.
status: Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system was reported in 2025; continuous replenishment plus full error-corrected computation is a stronger target.
why: Atom loss must become a recoverable service event rather than a run-ending failure.
key_works: Neng-Chun Chiu et al. (2025), *Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system*, arXiv:2506.20660.

title: Optical-power scaling of large atom processors
open: Increase array size and active-gate throughput without proportional growth in expensive laser power, intensity instability, scattered light, and cooling demand.
status: Large coherent arrays and rapid replenishment are demonstrated; affordable sustained optical operation is a separate scaling target.
why: Atom count is not the same as economically operable computational capacity.
key_works: Chiu et al. (2025), *Continuous operation of a coherent 3,000-qubit system*, arXiv:2506.20660.

title: Repeater advantage with finite memories and real latency
open: Exceed the appropriate repeaterless benchmark at useful rates after accounting for finite memory lifetime, heralding delay, multiplexing, local gates, and all unsuccessful attempts.
status: Capacity bounds define the target; partial repeater components do not demonstrate the complete rate advantage.
why: Determines whether entanglement can be distributed economically beyond direct-link limitations.
key_works: Pirandola et al. (2017), *Fundamental Limits of Repeaterless Quantum Communications*, arXiv:1510.08863.

title: Reliable zero-noise extrapolation under model mismatch
open: Produce calibrated uncertainty intervals when noise scaling changes the noise mechanism, circuit behavior, or drift trajectory rather than simply multiplying a fixed error rate.
status: Extrapolation methods exist; plausible curve fits do not guarantee valid zero-noise estimates.
why: Prevents systematically biased “corrected” experimental results.
key_works: Zhenyu Cai et al. (2023), *Quantum Error Mitigation*, arXiv:2210.00921; DOI:10.1103/RevModPhys.95.045005.

title: Scalable characterization of correlated gate errors
open: Recover the error features most relevant to logical computation with feasible experiments, without assuming that average gate fidelity determines them.
status: Benchmarking metrics capture selected operational quantities; many distinct correlated channels can share similar headline scores.
why: Reliable fault-tolerance predictions require more than one number per gate.
key_works: Proctor et al. (2017), *What randomized benchmarking actually measures*, arXiv:1702.01853; Bausch et al. (2024), *Learning high-accuracy error decoding for quantum processors*.

title: Asymptotic stabilizer rank of magic-state tensor powers
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Determine tight asymptotic exact and approximate stabilizer-rank growth for tensor powers of important resource states such as the T state.
status: Decomposition algorithms and lower bounds leave substantial uncertainty in the optimal exponential behavior.
why: Controls a major family of classical simulation algorithms for non-Clifford circuits.
key_works: Sergey Bravyi and David Gosset (2016), *Improved classical simulation of quantum circuits dominated by Clifford gates*, arXiv:1601.07601.

title: The general multipartite quantum entropy cone
subfield: Many-body structure, simulation resources, and sensing
open: Characterize all homogeneous entropy inequalities and achievable entropy vectors for general four-party and larger quantum states.
status: Stabilizer-state cones and other restricted families are better understood than the unrestricted quantum cone.
why: Governs possible information-sharing patterns and constrains coding and communication protocols.
key_works: Noah Linden, František Matúš, Mary Beth Ruskai, and Andreas Winter (2013), *The Quantum Entropy Cone of Stabiliser States*, arXiv:1302.5453.

title: R10-12. Unrestricted lower bounds for finding a welded-tree path
open: Prove an exponential quantum-query lower bound for outputting an explicit entrance-to-exit path in the standard randomly welded-tree oracle problem, or find a substantially faster path-output algorithm.
status: Quantum walks can find the exit efficiently without retaining a path. The 2023 “power of forgetting” result establishes a separation for a restricted class of genuine, rooted algorithms; the unrestricted path-finding question remains stronger.
why: Separates learning that an endpoint is reachable from producing an inspectable classical witness of reachability.
key_works: Andrew M. Childs, Matthew Coudron, and Amin Shiraz Gilani (2023), *Quantum algorithms and the power of forgetting*, arXiv:2211.12447; Scott Aaronson (2021), *Open Problems Related to Quantum Query Complexity*, arXiv:2109.06917.

title: R10-13. The PPT-squared conjecture beyond established special cases
open: Determine whether the composition of any two positive-partial-transpose quantum channels is entanglement breaking. A counterexample must give two valid PPT channels whose composition retains entanglement with a reference.
status: Qutrit and other structured cases are established. An August 2026 preprint reports finite entanglement-breaking index for every PPT channel, but eventual destruction under repeated composition is weaker than destruction after two PPT stages.
why: Determines how quickly successive bound-entanglement-compatible noise processes destroy all transmissible entanglement.
key_works: Sang-Jun Park (2026), *Every PPT channel has finite entanglement breaking index*, arXiv:2608.13551; Junhyeong An and Soojoon Lee (2026), *Beyond the Positive Partial Transpose Squared Conjecture: The Qutrit Case*, arXiv:2607.15947.

title: R10-15. Essential tensor-stable positive maps over ordinary complex numbers
open: Construct a finite-dimensional complex-linear map \(\Phi\) such that \(\Phi^{\otimes n}\) is positive for every positive integer \(n\), while \(\Phi\) is neither completely positive nor completely copositive; alternatively, prove none exist.
status: Nontrivial positivity for any prescribed finite number of tensor powers is possible. Constructions using nonstandard hypercomplex numbers do not settle existence over ordinary \(\mathbb C\).
why: Would clarify whether positivity can remain stable under unlimited composition without arising from the familiar completely positive structures.
key_works: Alexander Müller-Hermes, David Reeb, and Michael M. Wolf (2015), *Positivity of linear maps under tensor powers*, arXiv:1502.05630; Mirte van der Eyden, Tim Netzer, and Gemma De las Cuevas (2022), *Halos and undecidability of tensor stable positive maps*, arXiv:2110.02113.

title: R10-16. Decidability of tensor-stable positivity
open: Given an exactly specified finite-dimensional map with rational complex coefficients, decide whether all its tensor powers are positive, or prove that no algorithm can decide this for every input.
status: The 2022 analysis proves undecidability for a related matrix-multiplication-tensor positivity problem and develops connections to tensor-stable maps. It does not settle the ordinary all-tensor-powers decision problem.
why: Determines whether a complete automated classifier for this channel-related positivity property is possible.
key_works: Mirte van der Eyden, Tim Netzer, and Gemma De las Cuevas (2022), *Halos and undecidability of tensor stable positive maps*, arXiv:2110.02113; DOI:10.1088/1751-8121/ac726e.

title: R10-18. Joint dimension–accuracy optimality of diamond-norm channel tomography
open: Determine the sharp number of ordinary forward queries needed to learn an arbitrary noisy \(d\)-dimensional channel to diamond-norm error \(\varepsilon\). In particular, decide whether the general \(O(d^4/\varepsilon^2)\) dependence is jointly optimal when ancillas, collective measurements, and adaptive strategies are allowed.
status: The 2026 revision establishes optimal dimension and Kraus-rank dependence at constant accuracy, with upper bound \(O(d_{\rm in}d_{\rm out}k/\varepsilon^2)\). Matching separate parameter bounds do not automatically establish a matching joint lower bound.
why: Fixes the fundamental experimental cost of learning worst-case channel behavior rather than selected average observables.
key_works: Antonio Anna Mele and Lennart Bittel (2025/2026), *Optimal learning of quantum channels in diamond distance*, arXiv:2512.10214.

title: R10-23. Efficient capacity-achieving HSW square-root decoding
open: Construct efficiently described capacity-achieving codes for general finite classical–quantum memoryless channels whose Holevo–Schumacher–Westmoreland square-root decoding measurement has a polynomial-size implementation. Charge for codeword-state preparation, block encoding, conditioning, and measurement synthesis rather than assuming an exponential codebook oracle.
status: The coding theorem establishes existence of good measurements, not efficient circuits. Algorithms for Petz recovery and pretty-good measurements provide implementations under access and conditioning assumptions that need not remain efficient for HSW code families.
why: Converts a communication-capacity theorem into an executable receiver architecture.
key_works: Mark M. Wilde (2017), *Quantum Information Theory*, second edition, Section 20.3; András Gilyén, Seth Lloyd, Iman Marvian, Yihui Quek, and Mark M. Wilde (2022), *Quantum algorithm for Petz recovery channels and pretty good measurements*, arXiv:2006.16924; DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.128.220502.

title: R10-24. An unrestricted strong converse for blind mixed-state compression
open: For an arbitrary finite-dimensional source \(\rho^{AR}\), prove that reference-preserving reconstruction fidelity tends to zero whenever the compression rate is below \(S(CQ)\), where \(C,Q\) are the nonredundant Koashi–Imoto components. Allow arbitrary encoding and decoding channels.
status: The optimal first-order rate is established. The 2025 strong-converse revision proves results under additional decoder assumptions, rather than the unrestricted statement.
why: Determines whether operating below the fundamental rate causes complete failure, rather than merely preventing fidelity from approaching one.
key_works: Zahra Baghali Khanian and Andreas Winter (2022), *General Mixed State Quantum Data Compression with and without Entanglement Assistance*, arXiv:1912.08506; Zahra Baghali Khanian (2022; revised 2025), *Strong Converse Bounds for Compression of Mixed States*, arXiv:2206.09415.

title: R10-26. The entropy photon-number inequality for arbitrary independent inputs
open: For independent \(n\)-mode inputs \(A,B\) mixed on a beamsplitter of transmissivity \(\eta\), prove
status: Conjectured in 2007 and still discussed as open in a June 2026 specialist symposium. The established quantum entropy-power inequality and one-mode Gaussian optimizer theorems do not establish this full arbitrary-input statement.
why: Would provide sharp entropy constraints for optical mixing and strengthen capacity analyses of bosonic communication systems.
key_works: Giacomo De Palma, Andrea Mari, and Vittorio Giovannetti (2014), *A generalization of the Entropy Power Inequality to Bosonic Quantum Systems*, arXiv:1402.0404; Giacomo De Palma, Dario Trevisan, and Vittorio Giovannetti (2017), *Gaussian States Minimize the Output Entropy of One-Mode Quantum Gaussian Channels*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.118.160503.

title: R10-27. Minimum-output-entropy additivity with a nonunital qubit factor
status: Unital-qubit results and several other special classes are established. High-dimensional counterexamples to general additivity do not answer this qubit-factor question.
why: Identifies whether a single noisy qubit channel can participate in the entangled-input mechanisms responsible for entropy nonadditivity.
key_works: Christopher King (2002), *Additivity for unital qubit channels*, Journal of Mathematical Physics 43, 4641–4653; Alexander S. Holevo (2015), *Gaussian optimizers and the additivity problem in quantum information theory*, arXiv:1501.00652.

title: R10-28. Intermediate-\(p\) multiplicativity for identity-mixed Werner–Holevo channels
status: Multiplicativity at \(p=2\) is proved for the mixed family; the unmixed Werner–Holevo channel is understood for \(1\le p\le2\). These endpoint and boundary results do not cover the stated interior region.
why: Isolates a highly symmetric surviving test case after broad maximal-output-norm conjectures failed.
key_works: Spiros Michalakis (2007), *Multiplicativity of the maximal output 2-norm for depolarized Werner-Holevo channels*, arXiv:0707.1722; Nilanjana Datta (2004), *Multiplicativity of Maximal p-Norms in Werner-Holevo Channels for \(1\le p\le2\)*, arXiv:quant-ph/0410063.

title: R10-32. Infinite coherence cost without pairwise reversibility
open: Determine whether a Gibbs-preserving channel can require unbounded coherence for exact implementation by thermal operations even though it is **not pairwise reversible**—that is, no recovery channel can exactly restore any pair of orthogonal input states. Construct such a channel or prove that pairwise reversibility is necessary for divergent coherence cost.
status: Tajima–Takagi prove infinite coherence cost for a class of pairwise-reversible channels satisfying an additional energy-related condition. Their final 2025 paper explicitly leaves open whether every cost-diverging Gibbs-preserving channel must be pairwise reversible.
why: Identifies the physical mechanism behind thermodynamic operations that appear mathematically free but cannot be implemented with finite coherence resources.
key_works: Hiroyasu Tajima and Ryuji Takagi (2025), *Gibbs-Preserving Operations Requiring Infinite Amount of Quantum Coherence*, arXiv:2404.03479; DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.134.170201.

title: QMA versus QCMA
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Prove or disprove that polynomial-size quantum witnesses provide more verification power than polynomial-size classical witnesses for a quantum verifier.
status: The unrelativized question remains open. Classical-oracle separations were obtained in 2026; the older “find a classical-oracle separation” formulation is therefore not the remaining problem.
why: Identifies whether useful evidence can be intrinsically quantum.
key_works: John Bostanci, Jonas Haferkamp, Chinmay Nirkhe, and Mark Zhandry (2026), *Separating QMA from QCMA with a Classical Oracle*, STOC 2026.

title: The power of unentangled quantum witnesses
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Determine whether QMA(2), with two unentangled witnesses, equals QMA or is strictly more powerful.
status: The ordinary complexity-class question remains open. A September 2026 preprint establishes a quantum-oracle separation and resolves the associated no-disentanglers conjecture, not the unrelativized equality.
why: Determines how much computational power comes from a promise about independence.
key_works: John Bostanci et al. (2026), *A quantum oracle separation between QMA(2) and QMA*, arXiv:2609.02865.

title: The quantum PCP conjecture
subfield: Computational complexity and quantum proof systems
open: Prove or disprove QMA-hardness of approximating the ground-state energy density of bounded-locality, bounded-degree Hamiltonians to a constant additive accuracy.
status: Open. Good quantum codes, NLTS constructions, and recent locally testable-code claims do not themselves establish quantum PCP.
why: Determines whether extensive quantum entanglement remains computationally essential at nonzero energy density.
key_works: Dorit Aharonov, Itai Arad, and Thomas Vidick (2013), *The Quantum PCP Conjecture*, arXiv:1309.7495; Sevag Gharibian (2026), *Hardness of Approximation for Ground State Problems*.

title: Negative-partial-transpose bound entanglement
subfield: Quantum information, entanglement, and channel capacities
open: Establish whether a negative-partial-transpose state can remain undistillable for every finite number of copies.
status: Open. A July 2026 preprint solves the two-copy Werner-state problem, but explicitly leaves the arbitrary-copy endpoint problem unresolved.
why: Determines whether detectable entanglement can remain permanently unusable for singlet distillation.
key_works: Kishor Bharti, Rishikesh Gajjala, and Tobias Haug (2026), *Two-copy nondistillability of Werner states: sharp partial-trace inequalities and finite-copy extensions*, arXiv:2607.24479.

title: Exact quantum capacity of the depolarizing channel
subfield: Quantum information, entanglement, and channel capacities
open: Determine the quantum capacity of the qubit depolarizing channel throughout its nontrivial parameter range, including whether and where regularization is essential.
status: Open. Improved upper bounds, coding constructions, and strong-converse results do not yield the exact capacity curve.
why: Provides a fundamental benchmark for transmitting quantum information through symmetric noise.
key_works: Tulja Varun Kondra et al. (2026), *Sharp Quantum Capacity Thresholds: Exponential Strong Converses for Degradable and Antidegradable Channels*, arXiv:2608.01308; Zhiwei Song et al. (2026), *Approximate majorization and high-order capacity of quantum depolarizing channels*.

title: Exact output majorization for depolarizing channels
subfield: Quantum information, entanglement, and channel capacities
open: Prove or refute the exact output-majorization conjecture for tensor powers of depolarizing channels, beyond approximate majorization guarantees.
status: Open. September 2026 work proves approximate majorization and sharp higher-order consequences without resolving the exact conjecture.
why: Could tightly constrain the benefit of entangled inputs in channel coding.
key_works: Zhiwei Song, Xin Wang, Marco Tomamichel, and Kun Fang (2026), *Approximate majorization and high-order capacity of quantum depolarizing channels*, arXiv:2609.37240.

title: Polynomial-time dihedral hidden subgroup algorithms
subfield: Quantum query complexity and algebraic algorithms
open: Find a polynomial-time quantum algorithm for the dihedral hidden subgroup or dihedral coset problem, or prove meaningful limitations for broad algorithmic models.
status: Open. A claimed August 2026 solution was explicitly refuted; that algorithm cannot recover even the required secret bit with non-negligible advantage.
why: Would substantially change the quantum algorithmic landscape for lattice-related problems.
key_works: Andrew Childs and Wim van Dam (2010), *Quantum algorithms for algebraic problems*, arXiv:0812.0380; Aparna Gupte, Seyoon Ragavan, and Mark Zhandry (2026), *The ePrint:2026/1591 Quantum Algorithm Does Not Solve DCP*, ePrint:2026/1693.

title: R10-01. An eleven-qubit, three-logical-qubit code with weight-four checks
open: Determine whether an \([[11,3,3]]\) qubit stabilizer code admits eight independent commuting generators, each of Pauli weight at most four. Allow arbitrary connectivity and non-CSS constructions.
status: The 2026 low-weight-code analysis leaves the minimum possible maximum generator weight at **four or five**. Weight-five constructions exist; weight four remains unresolved.
why: Resolves a small, concrete check-complexity gap relevant to hardware-efficient error correction.
key_works: Fuchuan Wei, Zhengyi Han, Austin Yubo He, Zimu Li, and Zi-Wen Liu (2026), *Theory of low-weight quantum codes*, arXiv:2601.19848.

title: R10-02. The square-root distance conjecture for weight-four stabilizer codes
open: Prove or refute that every qubit stabilizer code encoding at least one logical qubit and generated by weight-at-most-four checks satisfies \(d=O(\sqrt n)\), **without assuming geometric locality**.
status: Explicitly conjectured in 2026. Weight-three generators impose much stronger limitations; weight-four toric-code families attain square-root distance.
why: Would identify an intrinsic check-weight obstruction, rather than a hardware-layout obstruction.
key_works: Wei et al. (2026), *Theory of low-weight quantum codes*, arXiv:2601.19848.

title: R10-03. An absolutely maximally entangled state of eight ququarts
open: Construct a pure state on \((\mathbb C^4)^{\otimes8}\) whose reduction to every four-party subset is \(I_{256}/256\), or prove that no such state exists.
status: The 2026 classification of seven-party absolutely maximally entangled states explicitly identifies **AME(8,4)** as a remaining existence problem. Settling seven-party cases does not settle this eight-party instance.
why: Supplies—or rules out—a particularly small perfect tensor with applications to erasure correction, secret sharing, and tensor-network constructions.
key_works: Fei Shi, Xiande Zhang, Qi Zhao, and Lvzhou Li (2026), *Complete Existence Classification of Seven-Partite Absolutely Maximally Entangled States*, arXiv:2608.01011.
aliases: AME(8,4); eight-leg perfect tensor of bond dimension four.

title: R10-04. Optimal length of permutation-invariant codes correcting \(t\) errors
open: Determine whether the shortest two-dimensional permutation-invariant qubit code correcting \(t\) arbitrary errors has length
status: The 2026 numerical study conjectures the equivalent distance bound \(n\ge(3d^2+1)/4\), with evidence of saturation. General constructions and numerical optima do not establish the proposed formula for every \(t\).
why: Determines the optimal redundancy when individual particles cannot be distinguished or addressed.
key_works: Liam J. Bond, Jiří Minář, Māris Ozols, Arghavan Safavi-Naini, and Vladyslav Visnevskyi (2026), *Permutation-invariant codes: a numerical study and qudit constructions*, arXiv:2603.10981; Arda Aydin, Max A. Alekseyev, and Alexander Barg (2024), *A family of permutationally invariant quantum codes*, Quantum 8, 1321.

title: R10-05. A seven-qubit code encoding three orthogonal states and correcting one error
open: Determine whether an arbitrary, potentially nonadditive \(((7,3,3))_2\) quantum code exists. Equivalently, find a rank-three projector satisfying all distance-three Knill–Laflamme conditions, or certify impossibility.
status: The March 2026 rational-certificate table still gives **\(2\le K_{\max}(7,3)\le3\)**. The upper endpoint is not known to be achievable.
why: Tests whether abandoning stabilizer structure improves one of the smallest single-error-correcting codes.
key_works: Gerard Anglès Munné and Felix Huber (2026), *SDP bounds on quantum codes: rational certificates*, arXiv:2603.19901.

title: R10-06. A nine-qubit, thirteen-dimensional, distance-three code
open: Construct a \(((9,13,3))_2\) code or prove that every nine-qubit code correcting one arbitrary error has dimension at most twelve. The search must include codes outside the codeword-stabilized framework.
status: A twelve-dimensional nonadditive code is known; the 2026 certified bounds remain **\(12\le K_{\max}(9,3)\le13\)**. Searches restricted to codeword-stabilized constructions do not exclude arbitrary codes.
why: Closes a longstanding one-dimension gap in a canonical nonadditive-code benchmark.
key_works: Sixia Yu, Qing Chen, C. H. Lai, and C. H. Oh (2008), *Nonadditive Quantum Error-Correcting Code*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevLett.101.090501; A. Rigby, J. C. Olivier, and P. Jarvis (2019), *Heuristic construction of codeword stabilized codes*, DOI:10.1103/PhysRevA.100.062303; Anglès Munné and Huber (2026), arXiv:2603.19901.

title: R10-07. Semi-Clifford normal forms for two odd-prime-dimensional qudits
open: Determine whether every two-qudit gate in every finite level of the Clifford hierarchy can be written \(U=C_1DC_2\), with Clifford \(C_1,C_2\) and diagonal \(D\), when the local dimension is an odd prime. The unresolved levels begin beyond the established third-level results.
status: The 2025 one-qubit-or-qudit classification does not settle two-qudit higher levels. Its concluding conjectures explicitly extend the normal-form question to two qudits.
why: Would provide systematic gate-teleportation and synthesis structures for higher-dimensional fault-tolerant computation.
key_works: Nadish de Silva and Oscar Lautsch (2025), *The Clifford hierarchy for one qubit or qudit*, arXiv:2501.07939; I. Chen and N. de Silva (2024), *Characterising semi-Clifford gates using algebraic sets*, Communications in Mathematical Physics 405, 201.

title: R10-10. Aaronson–Ambainis influence for all bounded low-degree polynomials
open: Prove or refute that every bounded multilinear polynomial \(p:\{-1,1\}^N\to[0,1]\), of degree at most \(d\) and variance at least \(\varepsilon\), has a coordinate of influence at least \((\varepsilon/d)^C\) for some universal constant \(C\).
status: Still open generally. September 2026 results obtain sharp inequalities for completely bounded polynomials and associated quantum algorithms; those additional structural assumptions do not cover every bounded polynomial.
why: Would explain why substantial quantum query advantages require exploitable structure rather than merely low polynomial degree.
key_works: Scott Aaronson and Andris Ambainis (2014), *The Need for Structure in Quantum Speedups*, Theory of Computing 10, 133–166; Francisco Escudero Gutiérrez, Miquel Saucedo, and Carlos Palazuelos (2026), *Optimal inequalities for completely bounded polynomials and the limitations of quantum query algorithms*, arXiv:2609.05201.

title: R10-11. Exact parity in higher-depth QAC⁰
open: Determine whether polynomial-size, constant-depth quantum circuits built from arbitrary one-qubit gates and unbounded-fanin Toffoli gates can compute parity exactly using polynomially many initialized ancillas. Unbounded fanout must not be supplied as a free primitive.
status: The 2025–2026 lower-bound work excludes exact parity at depth three even with unrestricted size and ancillas, and establishes approximation limitations at depth two. General higher constant depth remains unresolved.
why: Resolves whether genuinely quantum interference defeats the classical constant-depth obstruction to parity in this gate model.
key_works: Cristopher Moore (1999), *Quantum Circuits: Fanout, Parity, and Counting*; Malvika Raj Joshi, Avishay Tal, Francisca Vasconcelos, and John Wright (2025/2026), *Improved Lower Bounds for QAC0*, arXiv:2512.14643; DOI:10.1145/3798129.3800922.

title: R10-14. Absolute PPT versus absolute separability for two qutrits
open: Determine whether every \(3\times3\) bipartite state that remains PPT after every global unitary also remains separable after every global unitary.
status: Open for two qutrits. March 2026 work classifies relevant extreme points with three distinct eigenvalues, but does not establish equality of the full absolutely-PPT and absolutely-separable sets.
why: Tests whether the spectrum alone can conceal entanglement beyond all partial-transpose tests, even after arbitrary global basis changes.
key_works: Nalan Wang, Lin Chen, and Zhiwei Song (2026), *Extreme points of absolutely PPT states with exactly three distinct eigenvalues*, arXiv:2603.20717.

title: R10-19. Finite collapse of the exact PPT entanglement-cost hierarchy
open: Prove or refute Conjecture S33 of Lami–Mele–Regula:
status: The 2025 paper establishes efficient approximation through converging hierarchies and reports numerical support for collapse. Approximate computability is already established; universal exact collapse is not.
why: Would remove the remaining hierarchy limit from an operational entanglement-cost formula.
key_works: Ludovico Lami, Francesco A. Mele, and Bartosz Regula (2025), *Computable entanglement cost under positive partial transpose operations*, arXiv:2405.09613; Physical Review Letters 134, 090202, Supplemental Material, Conjecture S33.

title: R10-20. Sub-ebit implementation of the elegant joint measurement
open: Can a higher-Schmidt-rank pure resource state with entanglement entropy below one ebit implement the two-qubit elegant joint measurement exactly and deterministically by LOCC? Only its classical outcome must be produced.
status: One ebit suffices by teleportation. The 2026 analysis explicitly leaves the higher-rank, sub-ebit possibility open.
why: Tests whether extra resource dimension lowers the entanglement cost of a fixed distributed measurement.
key_works: Seiseki Akibue, Jisho Miyazaki, and Hiroyuki Osaka (2025/2026), *Optimizing Entanglement Manipulation via Algebraic-Geometric Decompositions and Semidefinite Programming Hierarchies*, arXiv:2501.17394.
aliases: EJM cost; symmetric joint measurement cost.

title: R10-21. A strict asymptotic distillation gap between SEP and PPT operations
open: Exhibit a bipartite state \(\rho\) for which \(D_{\rm SEP}(\rho)<D_{\rm PPT}(\rho)\), using asymptotic singlet rates with vanishing error. A single-copy success-probability gap is insufficient.
status: The 2026 analysis explicitly identifies this separation as unresolved despite progress on single-copy optimization.
why: Would show that the PPT relaxation overestimates asymptotically usable entanglement even relative to all separable operations.
key_works: Akibue, Miyazaki, and Osaka (2025/2026), *Optimizing Entanglement Manipulation via Algebraic-Geometric Decompositions and Semidefinite Programming Hierarchies*, arXiv:2501.17394, Section 5.5.

title: R10-29. A strict advantage of fully interleaved superchannel discrimination
open: In the realization-based superchannel-discrimination model, determine whether fully general causal interleaving can achieve a strictly better asymmetric error exponent than nested adaptive strategies. Supply an explicit pair exhibiting a gap, or prove equality under clearly stated access rules.
status: Hirche establishes achievable and converse quantities for several strategy classes, but leaves gaps between the general interleaved and more restricted formulations. Classical cases do not settle the quantum question.
why: Determines whether access to a process’s temporal structure has operational value beyond repeated use of the process as a single higher-order object.
key_works: Christoph Hirche (2023), *Quantum Network Discrimination*, arXiv:2103.02404; DOI:10.22331/q-2023-07-25-1064.

title: R10-30. Polynomial entanglement lower bounds for one-round quantum routing
open: Find an explicit efficiently computable Boolean family \(f_n(x,y)\) such that any constant-error, one-round simultaneous-message protocol routing an unknown qubit to the party selected by \(f_n\) requires initial entanglement of formation at least \(n^c\), for some \(c>0\).
status: The September 2026 revision of Bogner’s work proves an **\(\Omega(\log n)\)** entanglement-of-formation lower bound for inner-product routing, allowing arbitrary mixed shared resources and error at most \(0.09\). Polynomial lower bounds remain open.
why: Would establish substantial resource requirements for nonlocal quantum computation and strengthen the foundations of position-based cryptographic security.
key_works: Kevin Bogner (2026), *Robust logarithmic entanglement lower bound for f-routing*, arXiv:2608.05775v3; René Allerstorfer, Harry Buhrman, Alex May, Florian Speelman, and Philip Verduyn Lunel (2024), *Relating Non-Local Quantum Computation to Information Theoretic Cryptography*, Quantum 8, 1387.

title: R10-31. Causally faithful routed-circuit decompositions
open: Determine whether every finite-dimensional unitary admits a routed-circuit representation in which the absence of a permitted directed route exactly captures each operational no-influence relation. If not, characterize the obstruction and exhibit a minimal counterexample.
status: The September 2026 lattice-theoretic characterization advances ordinary unitary causal decompositions. Universal faithful realization using the richer routed-circuit formalism remains a separate target, also developed through thesis and workshop work.
why: Would connect experimentally meaningful causal independence to compositional circuit structure without introducing fictitious causal paths.
key_works: Tein van der Lugt and Robin Lorenz (2026), *Unitary causal decompositions: a characterisation via lattice theory*, arXiv:2508.11762; DOI:10.22331/q-2026-09-30-2218. Tein van der Lugt (2025), *Causal and Compositional Structure in Quantum Theory*, doctoral thesis, DOI:10.5287/ORA-VQ7OPD7AP. Augustin Vanrietvelde, Hlér Kristjánsson, and Jonathan Barrett (2021), *Routed Quantum Circuits*, arXiv:2011.08120.
